e-5419.knowledge_point: Determining the Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix Given the Number of Non-Pivot Columns
e-5419.problem: If $A$ is a $9 \times 11$ matrix that has $9$ pivot columns, then what is $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))?$
e-5419.worked_solution:
We know that $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $A$. 

Since $A$ has $11$ columns and $9$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is 

$$
11-9=2.
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))=2$.

e-5421.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is false. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(A))=1.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(B))=2.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$nd column). So, 

$$
\textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, only statement III is true.

e-5422.knowledge_point: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction
e-5422.worked_solution:
To find $\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ -6 & 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). 

Therefore,

$$
\textrm{nullity}(A) = \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A)) = 1.
$$

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

Recall that by definition, nullity(W)=dim(Null(W)).

To find dim(Null(W)), we reduce W to row echelon form, as follows:

W=[1−423−312495−20108]R2:=R2+3R1∼[1−4230010185−20108]R3:=R3(−5)R1∼[1−423001018000−7]

The reduced matrix has 3 pivot columns and 1 non-pivot column (the 2nd).

Therefore,

nullity(W)=dim(Null(W))=1.

content.worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))$, we reduce $W$ to row echelon form, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 12 & 4 & 9 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 5 & -20 & 10 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and  $1$
 non-pivot column (the $2$nd). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(W)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(W))=1.
$$
